verdict.headline: Three of the five operations do exactly what they claim and the derivation mechanics are flawless under both resolvers; the candidate fails because two rescoped sentences are still wrong about the checker in measurable ways, and one restated residual recites a fact that stopped being true before this candidate was authored. All three blockers are prose-sized repairs inside the existing five operations; no new mechanism is needed.

blockers.finding: The rescoped rule states the closure is computed 'BY FOLLOWING DIRECT NAME CALLS' and concludes 'The guarantee as stated: no DIRECT-SYNTAX consumer escapes the handler discipline'; the rescoped EV9-IR-01 closure states 'a fourth omitted site OF THE SAME DIRECT SYNTAX (direct-name calls, direct-name reachability) cannot recur silently as the third one did'. Both are falsified by measurement. _path_guard_scan builds its function table from subject.body filtered to ast.FunctionDef only (check-evidence-v10.py lines 3247-3248), so a definition in any of the three forms EV10-OBS-09 names (module-level AsyncFunctionDef, a FunctionDef nested inside a module-level if/try/with block, a ClassDef method) is not in the table, the walk cannot descend into it, and every consumption inside it is invisible EVEN WHEN the consumption is a direct ast.Name call to _path_steps and the function is reached from a checking entrypoint by direct name calls. Direct syntax plus direct-name reachability is NOT sufficient for visibility; the true bound is direct-name consumption inside module-level plain FunctionDefs reached through direct-name calls that resolve to module-level plain FunctionDefs.
blockers.measurement: In a disposable copy of the tree I added, at module level, `if True:` enclosing `def _ev11_probe_helper(row): _ = _path_steps(row.get('path', ''))` (an unguarded candidate-supplied consumption of the exact direct syntax the scan recognises), plus a direct name call `_ev11_probe_helper(row)` inside _grammar_delta_findings gated on two simultaneously-hostile positions, replicating the review's additive protocol. python3 -I -B artifacts/check-evidence-v10.py produced output BYTE-IDENTICAL to the unmodified baseline (same 4 environment findings, no PR-23 finding, scan counters unchanged). A fourth omitted site of the same direct syntax recurred silently, against the rescoped sentence's exact words. This is EV10-OBS-09's class, present in the same review whose findings this candidate disposes, and it is dropped by the rescope.
blockers.requiredRepair: Either (a) rescope once more, naming the definition-form bound: the guarantee covers direct-name consumptions lexically inside MODULE-LEVEL PLAIN FUNCTION DEFINITIONS reachable through direct-name calls between such definitions; consumptions inside async definitions, block-nested definitions and class methods are outside the scan's reach (EV10-OBS-09) and governed by review; or (b) bind EV10-IR-01 requiredRepair item 4 (extend the reachability walk to the three missed definition forms) onto the successor instrument alongside the exit-code obligation, and say in the rule that the current instrument does not cover them.

blockers.finding: The corrected closure ends: 'a dispatch reached without a compared flag literal is outside the scan's reach'. False in the direction of understating the instrument, and this corpus's EIR lineage standard is that a caveat is a measurement. _selftest_entrypoint_scan counts every ast.Call whose func is the ast.Name 'selftest' outside the selftest definition, independent of any flag literal, and the pinned predicate requires dispatchCount == 1 and guardedDispatchCount == 1 (check-evidence-v10.py lines 1605-1606). A second DIRECT dispatch with no compared flag literal anywhere is therefore inside the scan's reach and is reported twice over. The evasion the review actually measured requires avoiding BOTH a compared flag literal AND the direct name (its covert variant aliased the callee). The sentence as written tells a future author the scan is weaker than it is and misstates where the residual hole lies.
blockers.measurement: In a disposable copy I inserted into main(), after the guarded dispatch, `if len(flags) < 0: return selftest(candidate, source, authority, path)` — a second direct dispatch, runtime-unreachable, zero string literals, no compared flag. The run produced TEN new findings versus baseline, including 'main() dispatches to the selftest suite 2 time(s); exactly one dispatch is permitted' and 'a dispatch to the selftest suite is not guarded by a declared flag', plus the SB-19 predicate failures. The dispatch was emphatically not outside the scan's reach.
blockers.requiredRepair: Replace the clause with the measured boundary: 'a dispatch that avoids both a compared flag literal and the direct name selftest — an aliased or otherwise indirect call gated without a comparison — is outside the scan's reach (retainedResiduals[13])'.

advisories.note: retainedResiduals[13] ('a future author who reaches a path consumer or a flag dispatch through any indirection gets a green run from both scans') is faithful to EV10-IR-R8's own words, so this is graded advisory, but both halves are imprecise as measured. For the flag scan, indirection alone does not yield green: an aliased dispatch gated by a COMPARED undocumented literal is still reported through the flags-set equality; green requires evading the Compare collection AND the direct name together. For the path scan, per EV11-IR-01 no indirection is needed at all — a fully direct route through a missed definition form is also green. The next generation should restate the residual to the measured boundaries rather than carry R8 verbatim.
